dial.summary: DXY recovered from its July 31 intraday low of 99.87 to close at 100.19—crossing back above the headwind threshold—while real yields eased modestly to 2.37% from 2.41% peak; BTC Accumulation thesis holds: BTC.D firm at ~56.6%, BTC at $64,846, TOTAL at $2.26T, global M2 expanding at $102.7T—ISM PMI July print (August 3) and NFP (August 7) are the next key tests for the macro pivot thesis.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro 4-bank aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) June 2026 confirmed at $102.7T; July 2026 global aggregate not yet published, but US M2 rose to $23.3T in July (up from $23.2T in June, +6.1% YoY), China M2 ~$49.96T—all four central banks recording monthly gains; 4-week trend up (June > May, July component data expanding YoY at ~6% for US); status supportive (4-week uptrend intact; YoY contracting headwind condition not met).

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: June 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI remains the latest confirmed read at 53.3% (released July 1)—sixth consecutive expansion month, down 0.7pp from May's 54.0%; July 2026 ISM print releases August 3 at 10:00 AM ET; S&P Global US Manufacturing flash PMI for July at 53.8 (vs 53.9 in June) provides advance signal of continued expansion at a modestly slower pace; 4-week trend down (54.0% May → 53.3% June, -0.7pp); status neutral (above 50 but falling—supportive requires above 50 AND rising).

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY closed July 31, 2026 at approximately 100.19, recovering from an intraday low of 99.87 (set during Japan FX intervention) after the BOJ held at 1.0% and USD/JPY rebounded toward 160; the close above 100 restores headwind status; 30-day trend: ~101.34 (July 1) → 100.19 (July 31) = -1.15%, clearly above the 0.5% flat threshold, trend down; status headwind per ICE DXY spot threshold (above 100); DXY needs to sustain a break below 100.00 and approach 97.5 to transition to neutral or supportive.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: DFII10 (10-year TIPS real yield) at 2.37% as of July 31, 2026, down from the 2.41% peak on July 29 following soft Q2 GDP (1.5% vs 2.1% est) and core PCE (0.1% MoM vs 0.2% est); 4-week trend up: ~2.18% (June 30) → 2.37% (July 31) = +19bps, well above the 5bps flat threshold; status headwind (above 2% and rising over 4-week period; September FOMC pivot remains the primary real-yield compression catalyst).

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: July 31, 2026: 10-year Treasury 4.74%, 2-year Treasury 4.29%; spread = +0.45% (up 1bp from +0.44% prior run); 4-week change: +5bps from June 30 spread of ~+0.40%, right at the steepening threshold; trend flat (marginal change does not confirm sustained steepening); status neutral (positive spread, minimal steepening; not deeply inverted; supportive requires positive AND steepening).

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL at $6,738B ($6.74T) for week ending July 29, 2026 (H.4.1 released July 30, 2026): $4,516B Treasuries + $1,945B MBS + remaining other assets; prior week (July 22) was $6.75T; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.72T (week ending June 24) → $6.74T (July 29) = +$0.02T (+0.30%), within the <0.5% flat threshold; status supportive (flat to marginally growing; QT effectively paused; no aggressive runoff with rising overnight rates).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: CoinGlass returned HTTP 403 again this run; value carried forward at +0.004%/8h (annualized ~+4.4%)—well below the 0.04%/8h overheating threshold; BTC price at ~$64,846 (July 31 close), up modestly from $64,256 prior run, consistent with a low-leverage spot-led market; no evidence of funding spike despite BTC.D holding near 56.6%; 30-day trend down (from ~+0.006%/8h in late June); status supportive (near-zero funding far from overheating).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$302B (USDT ~$184B, USDC ~$74.89B); total crypto market cap $2.26T (BTC ~$1.28T, BTC.D ~56.6%); dominance: $302B / $2.26T = 13.36% ≈ 13.4%; 30-day trend down: TOTAL grew from ~$2.1T (July 1) while stablecoin dominance compressed from ~15% to 13.4%—capital rotated from stablecoins into risk assets on 30-day basis; status supportive (falling on 30-day basis; TOTAL up significantly over 30 days while stablecoins contracted).

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Manufacturing PMI for July 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—first Q3 manufacturing activity read and the most anticipated US macro print of the week; prior June reading: 53.3% (sixth consecutive expansion month, -0.7pp from May's 54.0%); S&P Global US Manufacturing flash PMI for July edged down to 53.8 from 53.9, offering a cautious advance signal; markets will watch new orders (June: 56.0%) and prices paid (June: 73.0%); a print above 54 with declining prices paid would reinforce the soft-landing thesis and support BTC Accumulation; a miss below 52 would shift sentiment toward growth risk.

upcoming.title: JOLTS Job Openings (June 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for June 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—key labor demand gauge arriving one day after the ISM Manufacturing print and three days before the July NFP; macro context: soft Q2 GDP (1.5%), soft core PCE (0.1% MoM), BOJ held at 1.0% (July 31); a reading below 7.5 million openings would reinforce the soft-landing thesis and strengthen the September rate pause case, adding downward pressure on real yields (currently 2.37%).

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (July 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Services PMI for July 2026 at 10:00 AM ET—companion to the August 3 Manufacturing print; prior June 2026 reading: 54.0% (24th consecutive expansion month, -0.5pp from May's 54.5%); employment 51.2%, prices 67.7%; July reading is the second Q3 services data point framing September FOMC rate expectations; a reading above 54 with continued price moderation would reinforce the September pause case and add to the case for DXY sustained break below 100.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 2, 2026)
upcoming.note: Weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET—the weekly labor market pulse released one day ahead of the July NFP (August 7); a print near or above 260k would reinforce soft labor market signals and add to the September rate pause case; context: BOE held at 3.75% (July 30, 6-3 vote), BOJ held at 1.0% (July 31), and the hawkish July FOMC dissent keeps claims data elevated in market significance.

upcoming.title: Employment Situation / NFP (July 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for July 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—nonfarm payrolls, unemployment rate, and average hourly earnings; the primary labor market read ahead of the September FOMC; macro backdrop: soft Q2 GDP (1.5%), soft core PCE (0.1% MoM), DXY at 100.19 (headwind territory), real yields 2.37%; a weak NFP would open the door to September cut discussion, compressing real yields and extending DXY's 30-day downtrend; a strong print with hawkish FOMC dissenters would complicate the rate pause narrative.
